questions.q: What does `app.get("/", (req, res) => { res.json({ status: "ok" }) })` do?
options: Registers a route that responds to GET requests at "/" with a JSON body
Starts the server listening on a port
Installs the express package
Deletes all other registered routes
questions.explain: app.get registers a handler for GET requests at the given path; res.json sends the given object as a JSON response with the correct Content-Type header.

questions.q: In the route `app.get("/balance/:address", ...)`, where does the value of `:address` end up inside the handler?
options: In req.body
In req.params.address
In process.env.address
It is discarded unless explicitly parsed with JSON.parse
questions.explain: Express captures named route segments (prefixed with :) into req.params, so :address in the path becomes req.params.address inside the handler.

questions.q: Why does the balance route call `isAddress(address)` before calling `provider.getBalance(address)`?
options: To validate the HTTP input before ever touching the network, the same discipline applied earlier to environment variables and typed values — rather than letting a malformed address fail deep inside an RPC call
isAddress is required syntax for every Express route
isAddress encrypts the address for the RPC call
It has no real purpose, it's purely decorative
questions.explain: Validating untrusted input (here, HTTP request input) before it reaches the network call catches bad data early with a clear 400 response, instead of letting it fail confusingly further downstream.

questions.q: What determines that a particular `app.use((err, req, res, next) => {...})` function is treated as error-handling middleware by Express?
options: It must be registered before any other routes
It must be named "errorHandler"
It must be defined with exactly 4 parameters (err, req, res, next) and registered after all other routes
It must return a Promise
questions.explain: Express recognizes error-handling middleware specifically by its 4-parameter signature, and it must be registered after normal routes/middleware so errors passed via next(err) reach it.

questions.q: In an async Express route handler that calls `await provider.getBalance(address)`, what happens if that call throws and the error isn't caught or passed to `next()`?
options: The request may hang or the error goes unhandled instead of producing the clean JSON error response the error-handling middleware is meant to send
Express automatically retries the RPC call three times
The server always restarts itself
res.json() is called automatically with the error message
questions.explain: Without a try/catch calling next(err), an error thrown inside an async handler doesn't automatically reach Express's error-handling middleware, so the clean JSON error response the lesson sets up never gets sent.
